defects.claim_says: 31 CFR 569.201 'still refers to the national emergency declared in E.O. 13984'; the rationale repeats that 569.201 refers to the emergency declared in this order.
defects.source_says: 31 CFR part 569 is the Syria-Related Sanctions Regulations implementing EO 13894; its Note 5 reads 'section 3 of E.O. 13894, or ... the national emergency declared in E.O. 13984', an evident misprint for 13894 (the section text itself reads 'national emergency declared in E.O. 13894'). EO 13984 declares no emergency; it takes additional steps under the EO 13694 emergency. A misprint in an unrelated regulation is not a current predicate for the IaaS order.

defects.claim_says: the U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 10802 refers to the emergency this order declared as continued on March 24, 2026 (no later event recorded)
defects.source_says: 22 U.S.C. 10802(d) (Pub. L. 119-111, div. A, title I, sec. 102, Sept. 18, 2026) is statute text, not only a note: it provides that sanctions and other measures under any Executive Order issued to address that emergency, 'as in effect on the day before September 18, 2026', 'shall remain in effect'. The claim omits this legislative event and its effect on the order's legal basis before the cutoff.
